items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And so in time, Louis went to work... Jimmy Noon, he would play the 12 o'clock with Dr. Cook's 26 piece band... And so anyhow she got... And we had, of course in this band was Jimmy Noon, Rob Palmer, Freddie Kepa.

ctx.x: Well, what about before you went to school? Did you hear any music?

Yeah. Well, sometime my mother would have a fish fry and she was engaged with Roy Palmer. He had a friend that played a mountain. Later on you know Roy Palmer played baritone, cornet, trombone, a lot of instruments. He was a pretty good teacher. He taught a lot of people around Chicago, including myself and Lionel Hampton and Oscar Bunny Young, who I later played with at the Wisconsin Roof for about six years. And McKinley Thomas and Baritone, we had a band around there, including the singing brothers, Homer and…

Where was Eddie Atkinson from? New Orleans. I never heard of him down here. Oh, I've seen his greatest, he's buried out by Ron Wagamahema. Did he play with bass down here? Yeah, I think so, but not in early years. In early years.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Overnight Jimmy Noon was at the nest, right in the next block, the plantation on the corner, diagonally from the sunset. Then the sunset was right across the street. And he had the band.

ctx.x: Yeah, Kelly Stables. And Joe Oliver, he went in with Dave Payton at the plantation. So I visited first one place or another, and Louis Armstrong, by that time Louis left the band and went to New York to join Fletcher Henderson I think. And then Louis goes and joins Fletcher Henderson. And then Ori comes up to join Joe Oliver and he had Bob Schaffner and Tick Gray on trumpets. And he had the same Charlie Jackson on bass, bass horn, and he had Albert Nichols and Bonnie Bigard on the- and Darnell Howard. Well…
